mathgap.title: Signed 'has more than' interpretation
mathgap.principle: Interpret any phrase of the form 'X has more than Y' as a signed difference: if a numeric amount N is given, set X = Y + N; otherwise treat it as the equation X - Y = ... preserving the order of the names. This avoids turning a signed difference into an absolute value.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement uses 'has more than' either with a numeric amount or as part of a relational equation.
mathgap.example: Treating 'Eduardo has more than Carleigh' as |Eduardo − Carleigh| instead of the signed difference Eduardo − Carleigh.

mathgap.title: Conditional transfer handling
mathgap.principle: For statements of the form 'If X has more than N apples, X will transfer their apples to Y', first evaluate X's current count (after any prior updates). If the condition holds, move all of X's apples to Y (X becomes 0, Y gains X's previous count).
mathgap.example: Transferring Lyle's apples to Geoffrey even though Lyle only has 1 apple, ignoring the condition 'more than 3'.

mathgap.title: Increase by factor (including rational) interpretation
mathgap.principle: When a statement says 'the number of X increases by k times' (k may be a fraction), treat it as multiplication: new X = original X × k. This applies even when k is expressed as a rational number such as 64/45 or 13/10.
mathgap.example: Treating 'Mariah's apples increase by 64/45 times' as adding 64/45 apples instead of multiplying her original count by 64/45.

mathgap.title: Model transfers as net changes
mathgap.principle: When a transfer 'X gives N to Y' occurs, subtract N from X and add N to Y.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a transfer statement is present.
mathgap.example: Adding N to both X and Y instead of subtracting N from X and adding it to Y.

mathgap.title: Systematic equation solving
mathgap.principle: Introduce a variable for each person and translate every relevant statement into a linear equation, then solve the resulting system.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When multiple relational statements involve several people.
mathgap.example: Skipping the creation of variables and trying to guess numbers directly.

mathgap.title: Equal split and redistribution handling
mathgap.principle: If a person splits all their items equally among a set of recipients, set the splitter's final count to zero and give each recipient an equal share of the splitter's total.
mathgap.example: Leaving the splitter with some apples after a split‑all operation.

mathgap.title: Signed difference phrasing
mathgap.principle: Interpret 'difference between X and Y' as the signed difference X − Y, preserving the order given, rather than the absolute value.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement mentions the difference between two quantities.
mathgap.example: Treating 'difference between Newton and Mariah' as |Newton − Mariah| instead of Newton − Mariah.

mathgap.title: Include transfers as constraints before solving relational equations
mathgap.principle: Apply all transfer statements (including conditional transfers) first, updating each person's count, then use the resulting final counts when setting up and solving relational equations.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Before setting up and solving relational equations.
mathgap.example: Solving relational equations before applying a transfer that changes the involved counts.

mathgap.title: Direct counts as initial constraints
mathgap.principle: Treat direct count statements (e.g., 'X has N items') as the initial amounts before any transfers, splits, or other operations.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a direct count is given.
mathgap.example: Treating a direct count as the final count after later transfers.

mathgap.title: Answer formatting
mathgap.principle: Output the final answer using the exact required format: 'The final answer is $\boxed{<integer>}$'.
mathgap.example: Omitting the LaTeX box or using a different punctuation style.

mathgap.description: Treating direct count statements as final counts after transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model assumes a given count is already the final amount and ignores later operations that modify it.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Interpret direct counts as initial values, then apply all subsequent transfers, splits, and other changes before determining the final count.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model may leave the splitter with leftover items or fail to divide the total equally among recipients.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: When a split‑all statement appears, set the splitter's final count to zero and distribute the total equally among the listed recipients.

mathgap.description: Applying transfers in the wrong direction
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model may add the transferred amount to the source or subtract it from the target, reversing the intended flow.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: When a transfer 'X gives N to Y' occurs, subtract N from X and add N to Y.

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting 'increase by k times' as addition
mathgap.why_it_happens: The phrase 'increases by k times' can be read as adding k, but mathematically it means multiplication by the factor k.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Treat any 'increase by … times' statement as new = original × k, even when k is a fraction.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model may apply a transfer regardless of the stated condition or evaluate the condition using the wrong count.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: First evaluate the condition based on the current count; only if the condition holds should the entire source amount be moved to the target.
